findings.title: The archive example's tasks.md seeding is attributed to a requirement that states one seeding rule and nothing else
findings.recommendation: The reference sentence credits the tasks.md seeding to orbit-emit-composition's 'Payload schema references are proven by execution', whose Trail seeding paragraph (orbit/specs/orbit-emit-composition/spec.md:964) seeds ONE pass per formed_against token 'and nothing else' and sends any check reading state no example names to its residual. A round trip built to that baseline seeds no (User-validation task, so the archive example's deferral of 5.3 is refused (case 4, no task). The test's second rule (task 2.7) has no owner. Either carry that requirement in this change and add the second seeding rule beside the first, or reword the reference sentence so it no longer attributes the tasks.md seeding to that requirement, and record the uncovered rule as a named residual.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Carry orbit-emit-composition's 'Payload schema references are proven by execution' as a MODIFIED block that states the tasks.md seeding rule beside the trail rule. This is a third capability, at R-crc-1's ceiling.

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Point the reference sentence only at what the owner states, and name the tasks.md seeding as a test-local rule in design.md's Risks, leaving the baseline for a later carry.

findings.title: Bulk archive never tells the AI to write the per-change archive emit that is meant to carry its deferrals
findings.recommendation: Design D8 and the ADDED requirement both assume bulk archive 'then writes each change's archive emit, which the new write gate checks'. Bulk Step 8 (a sync, b mkdir+mv, c track outcome) never invokes /orbit:archive or orbit emit archive. The only mention of a per-change emit is the 'Scope: does NOT emit run-summary JSON' section (line 340), which asserts that each inner /orbit:archive invocation emits, while no step makes such an invocation. The new step composes deferred_validations 'for that change's own archive run summary', and the only orbit emit archive the body names is in the post-move repair sentence (line 307). An AI following Step 8 as written moves the change and writes no emit. The deferral is then lost and the write gate, the stage's 'impossible to forget' guarantee, never runs on the bulk path. Add a Step 8 sub-step, after 8b, that composes and runs orbit emit archive per change with its Step 3.2 deferrals, or point Step 8 at orbit-archive-change's Step 5.5. The gap is older than rc10, but rc10 is the first change whose record depends on that emit existing.

findings.title: On the bulk path the deferral brief arrives only after every move, so the user cannot abort on a weak why
findings.recommendation: On the single archive, the brief comes before the move (design Risk mitigation, design.md:43: 'the brief before the move ... put every deferral in front of the user'). In bulk, the dispositions are briefed only in the Step 9 summary, after every sync and move. The spec allows this, but the design's mitigation for 'a DEFERRED label can hide a weak reason' does not hold on that path. Either brief each change's dispositions before its 8a sync, as the fingerprint prompt already speaks per change, or state the post-move brief as a named limit in design Risks.

findings.title: Task 4.4 asserts a fact that exists only after the step that must dispose of it
findings.recommendation: Task 4.4's evidence is 'the archive emit is accepted by the write gate', which happens at Step 5.5, after the move. Step 3.2 must dispose of 4.4 before the move. OBSERVED would check the box before its evidence exists, so only DEFERRED (when: this archive's Step 5.5) is honest. The ADDED requirement already rules on the analogous case, 'A task whose assertion is about the baseline after sync is DEFERRED' (spec.md:57). Generalise that sentence to any assertion about post-move state (the emit, the archived directory), so the archiving session does not have to judge its own exit-(2) task case by case.

findings.title: Bulk archive has no gate prompt, so the defect rc10 closes for /orbit:archive persists through /orbit:bulk-archive
findings.recommendation: The new paragraph says 'The archive workflow's gate prompt SHALL read every reviewed gate'. The bulk-archive body has no gate prompt at all; it reads no gates[] row. An unapplied change bulk-archived past an unpassed review-proposal, the rc03a/rc13 shape, still records no decision. Out of scope at two capabilities, but neither the requirement nor design Risks names it. Add a named limit beside the hand-checked-tasks limit, or open a question for a later stage.

commentary: Probed the engine side by reading checkDeferredValidations against the DEFERRAL REFUSALS production case by case: cases 1-7, the missing-file rule and the empty-array-as-absent rule all match. parseCheckboxes' new ungrouped collection only catches lines before the first ## group, and that is exactly case 3's domain. A later H1 keeps the last group current, so such lines are keyed rather than lost. Superseded and blocked handling in Step 3.4 matches the live status JSON shape: `superseded` is present only when true, and the current change's own review-proposal row shows it. validate --strict passes, the scenario map reads 33 delta scenarios with 0 uncovered, and the touched suites are green (747 tests over the emit, round trip, parity, templates and parsers). I did not run the full suite or invoke audit-drift as a library; Pass 6 was a targeted grep of the templates and baselines for single-gate archive wording. The pattern behind the findings is the bulk path. The single archive is carefully built; bulk archive inherits the rule by reference, but its body lacks two steps the rule assumes: an emit write, and a gate prompt.
passes_skipped: 4: no perspectives defined (orbit/lenses/ absent); skip Pass 4
5: no critical paths defined (orbit/lenses/ absent); skip Pass 5

direction.reasoning: The engine half is correct and well tested, and the single-archive seam does what the stage set out to do: every reviewed gate that has not passed speaks, and every user-validation task is either closed with evidence or deferred with a reason the write gate checks. The two warnings are about where the record and the rule live, not about wrong behaviour on the primary path. Repair the reference's pointer to the seeding owner, and either give bulk archive its missing emit step or name that gap. Neither needs a redesign, and both are small enough to walk before archive.
